position: Thesis student· PhD Candidate in Geological Sciences
summary: My research examines the fluvial dynamics and morphological evolution of the Biobío, Laja, and Duqueco rivers through multitemporal remote sensing analysis of channel configuration, sediment bars, and surface water extent. It aims to identify river reaches susceptible to morphological adjustment in response to floods and extreme climatic events and to assess the effects of aggregate extraction on channel morphology and fluvial dynamics.
keywords: Impacts of Aggregate Mining on River Morphodynamics
name: Angela E. Contreras Gatica

position: Thesis student · Master's student in Forestry
summary: Forest engineer focused on integrating computational methods, remote sensing and artificial intelligence to study forest and environmental systems. His work explores hydrological modeling, hyperspectral imagery, LiDAR, point clouds, 3D reconstruction and machine learning for environmental analysis and digital plant phenotyping.
name: Bastián A. Rivas Maldonado

summary: Geologist focused on fluvial geomorphology, sediment transport and remote sensing. His research integrates multitemporal satellite imagery, geospatial analysis and field observations to study river dynamics and environmental change. His previous work examined the morphological evolution of the Laja River, while his current research focuses on the spatial and temporal variability of sediment transport in the Biobío River and its relationship with hydrological and morphological dynamics.
